body.en:
Why Successive Percent Changes Multiply Rather Than Add: An increase of \(p\%\) multiplies an initial quantity \(V_0\) by the growth factor \((1 + \frac{p}{100})\), and a subsequent decrease of \(q\%\) multiplies that new result by \((1 - \frac{q}{100})\):

\[ V_{\text{final}} = V_0 \left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\left(1 - \frac{q}{100}\right) = V_0 \left(1 + \frac{p - q}{100} - \frac{pq}{10{,}000}\right) \]

Because the second percent change applies to the updated base \(V_0(1 + \frac{p}{100})\) rather than the original base \(V_0\), the cross-term \(-\frac{pq}{10{,}000}V_0\) ensures that a \(20\%\) increase followed by a \(20\%\) decrease yields \(1.20 \times 0.80 = 0.96V_0\) (a net \(4\%\) decrease, never \(0\%\)).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations

On an architectural blueprint, a scale of 0.5 inches represents an actual distance of 6 feet. What actual distance, in feet, is represented by a line 3.5 inches long on the blueprint?
question.ar:
حل المسألة التالية في (Ratios, Rates, Proportions, Percentages & Scatterplots): Level 1 · Foundations

On an architectural blueprint, a scale of 0.5 inches represents an actual distance of 6 feet. What actual distance, in feet, is represented by a line 3.5 inches long on the blueprint?

solution.en:
Set up a proportion where \( x \) is the actual distance in feet:

\[ \frac{0.5\text{ in}}{6\text{ ft}} = \frac{3.5\text{ in}}{x\text{ ft}} \implies 0.5x = (3.5)(6) = 21 \implies x = \frac{21}{0.5} = 42\text{ feet}. \]
solution.ar:
Set up a proportion حيث \( x \) is the actual distance in feet:

\[ \frac{0.5\text{ in}}{6\text{ ft}} = \frac{3.5\text{ in}}{x\text{ ft}} \implies 0.5x = (3.5)(6) = 21 \implies x = \frac{21}{0.5} = 42\text{ feet}. \]

label.en: ⚠️ SAT Traps & Pitfalls — Rates, Percentages & Data Analysis
label.ar: ⚠️ SAT Traps & Pitfalls — Rates, Percentages & Data Analysis (النسب والمعدلات والتناسب والنسب المئوية ومخططات الانتشار)

body.en:
• Percent Change Base Denominator: \( \text{Percent Change} = \frac{\text{New} - \text{Old}}{\text{Old}} \times 100\% \). The denominator is always the original starting value. If an item drops from \( 80 to \)60, the percent decrease is \( \frac{20}{80} = 25\% \), NOT \( \frac{20}{60} = 33.3\% \).
  • Square and Cubic Unit Conversions: Linear conversions must be raised to the appropriate power. \( 1\text{ yard} = 3\text{ feet} \implies 1\text{ sq yard} = 3^2 = 9\text{ sq feet} \).
  • Residual Sign: \( \text{Residual} = \text{Actual } y - \text{Predicted } \hat{y} \). Points above the line of best fit have positive residuals; points below have negative residuals.
  • Causation vs. Association: Only randomized experiments can establish cause-and-effect. Observational surveys can only demonstrate correlation/association.

body.en:
Problem: A trend line for study hours \( x \) and score \( y \) is \( \hat{y} = 7x + 45 \). A student studied 5 hours and scored 84. What is the residual?

Solution: Predicted score: \( \hat{y} = 7(5) + 45 = 80 \). Actual score: \( y = 84 \). \[ \text{Residual} = y - \hat{y} = 84 - 80 = +4. \]
body.ar:

question.en:
Level 2 · Medium

A retailer reduces the price of a winter jacket by 25%. Two weeks later, the retailer reduces the sale price by an additional 20%. The final price is \$2. What was the original price of the jacket before any discounts?
question.ar:
حل المسألة التالية في (Ratios, Rates, Proportions, Percentages & Scatterplots): Level 2 · Medium

A retailer reduces the price of a winter jacket by 25%. Two weeks later, the retailer reduces the sale price by an additional 20%. The final price is \$2. What was the original price of the jacket before any discounts?

solution.en:
Let \( P \) be the original price. After the first 25% discount, the price is \( P(1 - 0.25) = 0.75P \). After the additional 20% discount on the sale price, the multiplier is \( (1 - 0.20) = 0.80 \):

\[ (0.80)(0.75)P = 96 \implies 0.60P = 96 \implies P = \frac{96}{0.60} = 160. \]

The original price was \$2.

\[ (0.80)(0.75)P = 96 \implies 0.60P = 96 \implies P = \frac{96}{0.60} = 160. \]

The original price was \$2.

body.en:
Problem: A container has a volume of \( 4 \text{ cubic yards} \). What is the volume of the container in cubic feet?

Solution: Since \( 1\text{ yd} = 3\text{ ft} \), the volume conversion factor must be cubed: \[ 1\text{ yd}^3 = (3\text{ ft})^3 = 27\text{ ft}^3. \]\[ 4\text{ yd}^3 \times 27\frac{\text{ft}^3}{\text{yd}^3} = 108\text{ cubic feet}. \]
body.ar:
Problem: A container has a الحجم of \( 4 \text{ cubic yards} \). What is the الحجم of the container in cubic feet?

Solution: Since \( 1\text{ yd} = 3\text{ ft} \), the الحجم conversion factor must be cubed: \[ 1\text{ yd}^3 = (3\text{ ft})^3 = 27\text{ ft}^3. \]\[ 4\text{ yd}^3 \times 27\frac{\text{ft}^3}{\text{yd}^3} = 108\text{ cubic feet}. \]

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced

A researcher randomly assigns 50 students to a tutoring programme and 50 to a control group, then compares test scores. Which conclusion is best supported if the tutored group scores significantly higher?

(A) Tutoring causes higher scores for the population sampled.
(B) There is an association, but causation cannot be determined.
(C) Results apply to all high school students nationwide.
(D) The sample size is too small to draw any valid conclusion.
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced

A researcher randomly assigns 50 students to a tutoring programme and 50 to a control group, then compares test scores. Which conclusion is best supported إذا كان the tutored group scores signإذا كانicantly higher?

(A) Tutoring causes higher scores for the population sampled.
(B) There is an association, but causation cannot be حدّدd.
(C) Results apply to all high school students nationwide.
(D) The sample size is too small to draw any valid conclusion.

solution.en:
Correct Answer: (A).

Because participants were randomly assigned to the treatment and control groups (a randomized controlled experiment), a causal conclusion can be established. Because the sample was drawn from a specific student population, the result generalizes to that sampled population (not nationwide, eliminating C).

body.en:
Problem: A rectangular solar array has an area of \( 18\text{ square yards} \). What is its area in \( \text{square inches} \)? (\( 1\text{ yard} = 3\text{ feet} \), \( 1\text{ foot} = 12\text{ inches} \)).

Solution: Since \( 1\text{ yard} = 36\text{ inches} \), squaring the linear conversion factor gives \( 1\text{ yd}^2 = 36^2\text{ in}^2 = 1,296\text{ in}^2 \). Multiply by 18: \[ 18 \times 1,296 = 23,328\text{ square inches}. \]

question.en:
Level 4 · Synthesis

Store A reduces the price of a jacket by 20% and then applies an additional 15% clearance discount to the reduced price. Store B reduces the same jacket by a single flat discount of \( d\% \). If both stores end up charging the exact same final price before tax, what is the value of \( d \)?
question.ar:
Level 4 · Synthesis

Store A reduces the price of a jacket by 20% and then applies an additional 15% clearance discount to the reduced price. Store B reduces the same jacket by a single flat discount of \( d\% \). إذا كان both stores end up charging the exact same final price before tax, ما قيمة \( d \)?

solution.en:
Multiply the two retention factors at Store A:

\[ (1 - 0.20)(1 - 0.15) = 0.80 \times 0.85 = 0.68. \]

A final multiplier of \( 0.68P \) corresponds to a single total discount of \( 1 - 0.68 = 0.32 = 32\% \), so \( d = 32 \).
solution.ar:
Multiply the two retention حلّلs at Store A:

\[ (1 - 0.20)(1 - 0.15) = 0.80 \times 0.85 = 0.68. \]

A final multiplier of \( 0.68P \) corresponds to a single total discount of \( 1 - 0.68 = 0.32 = 32\% \), so \( d = 32 \).
